title: SG-5.1 Rebuild HeaderOverlay on the kit
summary: HeaderOverlay becomes a wood bar with brass corners built on the frame kit, with every control the Done-when lists.
description: Context: HeaderOverlay (game/frontend/src/components/HeaderOverlay.tsx) already shows StoryForge, the world title, round id, status, Countdown, a Retry button on error, and sound and settings buttons wired to useUiStore. It is unstyled text inside .sf-frame-bar. The Suggest What Happens Next button is a separate frame button in App.tsx. Desired behavior: the header shows a gold logo, a world-name plaque, a status pill with dot and round id, the countdown, a gold + SUGGEST WHAT HAPPENS NEXT button that opens the contribution dialog, and sound and settings icons. Expected result: the header reads real round data and the old standalone Suggest button is gone. Why: the SG-5 goal replaces the placeholder look with the framed interface.
acceptance_criteria: Given a loaded round, when the header renders, then it shows the logo, the world-name plaque, a status pill containing a status dot, the round id and the status, and the countdown timer.
Given the header is rendered, when the player clicks the gold suggest button, then the contribution dialog opens.
Given the round is loading, failed or missing, when the header renders, then the pill shows the loading, error with Retry, or no-active-round state.
Given the header is rendered, when the player clicks the sound or settings icon, then uiStore soundEnabled or settingsOpen changes.

in_scope: HeaderOverlay layout and styling on the frame kit
gold suggest button inside the header
preserve: Round and error props of HeaderOverlay

technical_constraints: Phaser stays on 3.90.x; React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind, Radix and Zustand stay.
Keep the Go API contracts and the contribution flow; no mock data in place of real API calls.
Colours come from the shared palette tokens; fonts are bundled npm packages; no downloaded art or CDN links.
Tests are unit tests with all dependencies mocked.
definition_of_done: All requirements are done and their Verify units pass.
non_functional: Keyboard operable buttons with accessible names
